ai.description: The Satpura Eyelid Gecko (Eublepharis satpuraensis) reaches 10–12 cm. It features a yellowish-brown body with dark, irregular bands and prominent, movable eyelids. Its tail is thick and segmented.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eublepharis satpuraensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bold dorsal pattern of dark brown blotches bordered by white, which lack the fine spotting seen in other species.
ai.habitat: *Eublepharis satpuraensis* inhabits rocky, forested terrain within the Satpura Range, typically found in dry deciduous habitats at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Satpura eyelid gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging from rock crevices after sunset to actively hunt insects across the rugged, rocky terrain of its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eublepharis satpuraensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eublepharis satpuraensis* is endemic to the Satpura Range in central India, primarily inhabiting the states of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra at moderate elevations.
